fingerprints.query: select id, title from articles where published = true order by id limit ? offset ?
select id, name, price from products where name ilike ? and active = true
update sessions set expires_at = now(), revoked = true
select id, email from users where lower(email) = ?
select * from orders where customer_id = ? order by created_at desc
select id, title from articles where published = true order by random() limit ?
insert into audit_log (user_id, action, created_at) values (?+)
select id, status from orders where id in (?+)
select count(*) from order_items where order_id = ?

QL001.title: SELECT *
QL001.description: Heuristic: the select list contains * or table.*, which reads every column and breaks covering indexes. It cannot know whether you really need all columns.

QL002.title: Unfiltered write
QL002.description: Heuristic: an UPDATE or DELETE has no top-level WHERE clause and touches every row. It is sometimes intentional (maintenance jobs) and statements starting with WITH are not inspected.

QL003.title: Leading-wildcard LIKE
QL003.description: Heuristic: LIKE/ILIKE with a literal pattern starting with %, which usually prevents B-tree index use. Patterns built at runtime (CONCAT, ||, parameters) are not detected.

QL004.title: Large OFFSET
QL004.description: Heuristic: a literal OFFSET (or MySQL LIMIT offset, count) above 1000; the database must read and discard all skipped rows. Offsets passed as parameters are not detected.

QL005.title: Random ordering
QL005.description: Heuristic: ORDER BY RAND() / RANDOM() sorts the whole result set; the cost grows with table size even when only a few rows are returned.

QL006.title: Function on filtered column
QL006.description: Heuristic: a column is wrapped in LOWER, UPPER, DATE, CAST, COALESCE or EXTRACT inside a WHERE/AND/OR comparison, which can prevent plain index use. An expression index may make it fine.

QL008.title: Unbounded SELECT
QL008.description: Heuristic: a non-aggregate SELECT ... FROM with no WHERE and no LIMIT returns every row. Fine for small lookup tables; statements starting with WITH are not inspected.
